To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the responsibilities of primary care in relation to genetics are not yet clear.
the role of genetics and the need for genetics education in primary care are shifting.
primary care providers, clinical genetics experts, and patients with genetic diseases have different perspectives on the role of genetics and the need for genetics education in primary care.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the educational needs and role of genetics in the context of primary care.
the role of genetics and the educational needs of primary care providers, with a focus on general practitioners and midwifers.
the development of educational programmes in genetics for primary care providers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the primary care providers' knowledge and skills in genetics should be improved.
genetics is an integral part of primary care and therefore, primary care providers must be prepared to deal with the impact of ongoing genetic advances on their daily practice.
genetics education in primary care should be a priority and should be integrated into the curriculum of both postgraduate and master training programmes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genetics education in the context of primary care is a priority for all stakeholders and that the educational needs of general practitioners and primary care providers are different.
there is a need for genetics education for primary care providers, especially general practitioners, to prepare them to deal with genetics in their daily practice.
the role of genetics is changing and that primary care providers need to be prepared to take on new responsibilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
primary care providers need to be better educated about the role of genetics and genomics and how to integrate it into the practice of family medicine.
the role of genetics is changing in primary care and that this change has to be reflected in the education of primary care providers.
primary care providers are aware of the need for genetics education, but the extent of the need varies between disciplines and specialties.
